notes: The source changes match the reference for both the zip and squashfs backends, and the docs addition fits the feature. The tests cover the default skip, `--links` listing with the suffix, a regular `.rclonelink` member staying a regular file, readback size versus content, and an end-to-end check that a hostile archive cannot write outside the destination.

The code changes match the reference exactly for both zip and squashfs. The tests cover skip-without-flag, the `.rclonelink` listing with target readback via `NewObject`, a regular member whose name ends in `.rclonelink`, and the hostile-archive escape end to end; the docs addition is relevant but goes slightly beyond what was strictly needed.

The production change is identical to the reference: it closes the dup'd file, guards against double close with ErrClosed, and serializes refcount, close and unlink under the map mutex. It also skips unlinking abstract sockets, and the added tests cover every review requirement, including concurrent close/relisten and abstract sentinel files.

The code change is identical to the reference: it closes the dup'd file, adds a CAS-guarded close under the mutex, unlinks only on the last reference, and skips abstract sockets. The added tests cover each review requirement: immediate close and unlink for both socket types, refcounting, double-close returning net.ErrClosed, the close/relisten race, and abstract sockets not unlinking a file of the same name.

The SNMP wrapper and plugin changes match the reference exactly. Its tests are good: they check that an open connection keeps its engine ID, that reconnecting a closed one resets it, and that a failed gather closes the connection. However, the patch also bundles an unrelated rewrite of MIB path loading (a custom mibDirFS, AppendFS, and silently skipping unreadable paths) with its own test, which alters a separate subsystem and badly hurts scope.

The SNMP recovery fix matches the reference exactly: closing the connection on error and resetting the USM engine ID on reconnect, with good tests in the wrapper and the plugin. But the patch also rewrites MIB path loading in mib_loader.go (custom fs.FS, silently skipping unreadable paths), which is unrelated to this issue, changes behavior, and should not ship in this patch.

Fixes the root cause by making cancelOneJob re-aggregate a caller from its children instead of writing it Cancelled, and wakes concurrency waiters after a cancel that updates no job. The tests are meaningful: nested callers with runner acknowledgement, and force-cancel waking a waiter. Minor imprecision: the caller is always returned as 'cancelled' even when its status did not change, and the emit fires on every no-op cancel, not only when the run status changed. The model test also builds a child whose ID is lower than its callers', which breaks the deepest-first ID invariant and leaves the `Len 3` assertion slightly loose.

Fixes the root cause by having cancelOneJob re-aggregate an expanded reusable caller from its fresh DB children instead of writing it Cancelled, and wakes concurrency waiters on a job-less settle; two nits: it emits whenever no job changed even if the run status did not change, and it reports the caller as cancelled even when its status is unchanged, but the nested-caller and force-cancel tests are strong.
